extras.name: Badminton House
extras.note: 1709 Britannia Illustrata plate ('one of the Seats of the Most Noble & Potent Prince Henry Duke of Beaufort'); the house and its formal park survive (National Trust); the second impression (RP-P-1949-370) is the documented duplicate drop; the point is the house's P625

extras.name: Temple Newsam
extras.note: Britannia Illustrata plate 42, 1707-09 ('the Seat of the Rt. Hon. ble Arthur Lord Ingram Viscount Irwin'); the house survives (National Trust). The Commons description is the Hepworth boilerplate followed by the plate's own title ('Showing Temple Newsam. The engraving is entitled: ...') - the 566 px 'Temple Newsam Kip.jpg' impression has an empty desc, this 3576 px file does not - and it agrees with the title verified from the British Museum M,21.42 and five other sources in all identifying particulars (checked 2026-10-13). The file's MediaInfo item carries no P180 from this VM (checked 2026-10-13, also on a file with a rich item), so the staged row ties by caption (the stored desc names the house); the point is the house's P625

extras.name: Burford House
extras.note: 1707 plate (Yale B2017.35.1, 'the House at Windsor, Belonging to his Grace Charles Beauclerck' - the duke of St Albans' house, Nell Gwyn's former house on the edge of Home Park); the house is GONE (sold to George III 1779, absorbed into the Royal Mews) but the view is locked to the standing Windsor Castle (Q42646) in the same view. No enwiki article ('Burford House' is a 4-way disambiguation with a red Windsor link; the house is described in the 'Nell Gwyn' article, which this row's wikipedia carries). The point is the Mews/Saint Alban's Street site from two geograph photos' WGS-84 EXIF (51.481051,-0.605551 / 51.480870,-0.605556; Nominatim 'Royal Mews, Windsor' 72 m from it, same street), ~325 m SOUTH of the castle's P625, checked 2026-10-13

files.desc:
Part of the Gott Collection at the Hepworth Gallery, Wakefield, West Yorkshire, England. The collection was originally held by Leeds industrialist William Gott, and sold in 1908 and 1912 after the 1906 death of William Gott's son John, bishop of Truro.
 
Showing Temple Newsam. The engraving is entitled: "Temple Newsam, the seat of the Rt Hon.able Arthur Lord Ingram Viscount Irwin in the West Riding of the County of Yorke, Governor of Scarborough and Ld L.nt of the North Rideing of York Shire." The title includes a coat of arms with the motto  Scuto amoris divini  (or "the shield of divine love
